reason: The 13 October exploratory search downloaded a Singapore Law Watch headlines index containing this exact child URL, but the extractor did not promote it and the old publication-window rule excluded coverage of the 7 October official event. The verified 8 October report is retained as secondary coverage of the canonical MAS finding without creating a duplicate regulatory event or changing its date.

supplement.summary: Sarah Koh's Straits Times report, republished by Singapore Law Watch, explains MAS's third-party AI expectations, including financial institutions' retained accountability, risk-appropriate transparency and testing, contingency arrangements and proportionate treatment of lower-materiality uses. It is secondary reporting and adds communication context; the official MAS Guidelines remain the evidential authority for the supervisory expectations.
supplement.title: Financial institutions must remain accountable for use of third-party AI tools: MAS
